prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1164; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort at the scene. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received from insured.

Entry 2: Contacted claimant by phone to introduce myself and explain the claims process. Claimant confirmed she is not represented by an attorney and prefers to handle the matter directly. Claimant describes lower back strain with stiffness when sitting for long periods. She has not yet seen a physician. Advised her of medical evaluation options and to keep records of all treatment and expenses.

Entry 3: Received police report. Reporting officer notes the at-fault driver admitted to looking at a phone before impact. Both vehicles show rear and front damage consistent with a low-to-moderate speed impact. Photos reviewed and filed. Vehicle inspection scheduled with an independent appraiser.

Entry 4: Claimant visited urgent care for lower back strain. Records received indicate a diagnosis of muscular strain with a recommendation for rest, over-the-counter pain relief, and follow-up with a primary care provider if symptoms persist. Requested full medical records and authorization to obtain them. Claimant signed the release form and returned it by mail.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. She reports improvement in back pain but continued stiffness in the mornings. She is still working light duty. Explained that the file remains open pending the medical follow-up and the appraiser's estimate. Set a reminder to reassess the injury status in two weeks and to confirm whether she plans to continue treatment with her primary care provider.
